state.help: Combines full scans and PR reviews and keeps itself up to date: anything that stops showing up is marked fixed, and anything that comes back is reopened.
state.help_image: Combines every scan of this image and keeps itself up to date: anything that stops showing up is marked fixed, and anything that comes back is reopened.
state.help_domain: Combines every web scan of this site and keeps itself up to date: anything that stops showing up is marked fixed, and anything that comes back is reopened.

lifecycle.label: Lifecycle:
lifecycle.excluded: Excluded: it's in a path an admin excluded. It doesn't count as open or block PRs.
lifecycle.excluded_pattern: Excluded: it's in a path an admin excluded ({{pattern}}). It doesn't count as open or block PRs.
lifecycle.unseen_one: Unverified since {{date}}: the last scan couldn't check it (its engine failed or didn't reach where it was). It stays open but doesn't count toward any indicator.
lifecycle.unseen_other: Unverified since {{date}}: {{count, number}} scans in a row couldn't check it (its engine failed or didn't reach where it was). It stays open but doesn't count toward any indicator.
lifecycle.unseen_rule_off: Unverified since {{date}}: the rule that found it ({{rule}}) is off in the scan settings, so its absence proves nothing. It stays open but doesn't count toward any indicator, until a scan with that rule on stops finding it.
lifecycle.unseen_engine_off: Unverified since {{date}}: {{engine}} is turned off in the scan settings, so its absence proves nothing. It stays open but doesn't count toward any indicator, until a scan with {{engine}} on stops finding it.
lifecycle.unseen_rule_changed: Unverified since {{date}}: the rule that found it ({{rule}}) has changed since, so its absence proves nothing. It stays open but doesn't count toward any indicator; if you know it's gone, mark it fixed.
lifecycle.unseen_configuration: Unverified since {{date}}: the scan's configuration changed, so its absence proves nothing. It stays open but doesn't count toward any indicator; if you know it's gone, mark it fixed.
lifecycle.unseen_unidentified: Unverified since {{date}}: the scan still finds a secret in the same file that can't be told apart from this one, because the value of one of them couldn't be read for certain. It stays open but doesn't count toward any indicator; if you know it's gone, mark it fixed.

exclusions.title: Excluded paths
exclusions.patterns_help: From the repository root, up to {{max}}. To exclude only one rule there, write its ID after the path with a space: tests/** generic-api-key. The ID is under each finding's title.
exclusions.reason_placeholder: Why (kept in the history), e.g. “Intentionally vulnerable samples for testing the rules”
exclusions.saved: Saved. It also applies to upcoming scans and PR reviews.
exclusions.dialog_help: For what isn't your product: tests, examples that are vulnerable on purpose, generated or third-party code. Nothing is deleted or hidden: their findings move to the Excluded tab with the path that excludes them, and stop counting as pending or blocking pull requests. Remove the path and they go back to Open.
exclusions.label: Paths to exclude, one per line
exclusions.reason_required: Why they are excluded (required, kept in the history)
exclusions.reason_needed: Say why these paths are excluded, in at least {{min}} characters: it stays in the history.

preview.nothing: Nothing moves with the current findings: none enter or leave Excluded. The paths also apply to upcoming scans and pull request reviews.
preview.excluded_one: With the current findings, {{count, number}} open finding moves to Excluded, where it stays in view:
preview.excluded_other: With the current findings, {{count, number}} open findings move to Excluded, where they stay in view:
preview.reopened_one: {{count, number}} excluded finding goes back to Open:
preview.reopened_other: {{count, number}} excluded findings go back to Open:
preview.title: What saving changes now

exclusions.dialog_help_image: For files in the image that aren't your application. Nothing is deleted or hidden: their findings move to the Excluded tab with the path that excludes them and stop counting as pending. Remove the path and they go back to Open.
exclusions.patterns_help_image: From the image's root, up to {{max}}: usr/share/doc excludes that folder and everything in it.

examples.title: Examples
examples.anywhere: Any testdata folder, wherever it is.
examples.files: The .md files directly in docs, not in its subfolders.
examples.rule: Only rule {{rule}} under {{path}}: a known false positive. Everything else there still counts.

repo_settings.title: Repository settings
repo_settings.secrets_help: Only for this repository, on top of the organization's settings, which stay as they are. For example: silence the test keys in tests/fixtures (under “In these paths”), turn off a rule that only makes noise, or detect your company's token format. A silenced secret isn't hidden: it's listed under Excluded with the setting that withheld it.
repo_settings.defaults_none: Defaults: Betterleaks and Trivy built-in rules.
repo_settings.defaults_where: The defaults are set in Policies
repo_settings.paths_hint: For tests, examples or third-party code. Their findings stay in view under Excluded, but don't count as pending or block pull requests.
repo_settings.paths_hint_image: For files in the image that aren't your application. Their findings stay in view under Excluded, but don't count as pending.
repo_settings.secrets_hint: To silence test values, turn off a rule that only makes noise or detect your own tokens. What you silence is listed under Excluded with the setting that withheld it.

description.open: It counts as pending again in the panel, tickets and SARIF.
description.in_progress: Someone is working on the fix. It still counts as pending.
description.false_positive: It stops counting as pending in this and future scans of the repository. The history records your user and the reason.
description.accepted: You take on the risk for a limited time: it stops counting as pending until the expiry date, then reopens on its own.
description.fixed: Marks it fixed without waiting for the next scan. Explain how it was fixed (PR, patch, deploy) so it's in the history. If the next scan finds it again, it reopens on its own.

placeholder.false_positive: e.g. The HTML comes from a static template and is sanitized with DOMPurify
placeholder.accepted: e.g. Not exposed to the internet; will be fixed in the Q4 migration
placeholder.fixed: e.g. Token revoked in Auth0 and removed from the README in PR #5

fix.title: How to fix it
fix.adapt: The example shows the pattern and its fix; adapt it to your code.
fix.basis: Built from your lockfile and the advisories, not from your code: check it fits your project before you apply it. Reverify confirms the result.

verify.running: Verifying: the scan is queued or running…
verify.fixed: Fixed ✓ · no longer found in the scan
verify.fixed_at: Fixed ✓ · no longer found in the scan from {{date}}
verify.present_at: Still present in the scan from {{date}}
verify.inconclusive: The scan was incomplete (an engine didn't run), so it proves nothing. Try again.
verify.failed: The verification scan failed. Try again.
verify.prompt: Already fixed it? Reverify: we scan the repository or image again and tell you whether it's still there.
verify.prompt_web: Already fixed and deployed? Reverify: we run the passive scan of the domain again and tell you whether it's still there.
verify.demo: Demo data: rescan it with “make demo”.
verify.open_pr: It comes from an open pull request, so it's verified on every push to the PR.
verify.imported: {{tool}} reported it, so only {{tool}} can tell whether it's gone: import a new full SARIF from it.

audit.mapping_note: The mapping to each control is indicative.
audit.title: Audit evidence report
audit.description: A concise PDF with scope, method, findings and their status, approved exceptions and sign-offs. Everything is optional: leave it as is to use the defaults.
audit.portfolio_scope: Every scanned repository in the organization, its coverage against GitHub (which ones lack a complete scan), open critical and high findings, and exceptions, in one document.
audit.exceptions: Include exceptions and decisions (accepted risks and false positives with their reason)
audit.disclaimer: This is technical evidence for the auditor, not an audit opinion or a certification. Review and sign it before you hand it over.

secret_rules.title: Secret detection
secret_rules.saved: Saved. It applies from the next scan.
secret_rules.dialog_help: The secrets you silence, the built-in rules you turn off and your own detectors. They apply to every repository scan and PR review.
secret_rules.custom_rules_help: Detectors for your own tokens, run in Betterleaks and Trivy. The finding takes your description as its title and, like every secret, is critical. Regular expressions use RE2 syntax: no lookarounds or backreferences.
secret_rules.disabled: Turn off a built-in rule that only makes noise
secret_rules.disabled_help: Turned off in Betterleaks and, when Trivy has the same detector, in Trivy too. Turn off only rules that produce noise you've already reviewed.
secret_rules.allow_regexes: When the value matches one of these expressions
secret_rules.allow_regexes_help: One per line, checked against the detected value (RE2: no lookarounds or backreferences). Up to {{max}}.
secret_rules.allow_paths_help: One per line, from the repository root, like excluded paths: fixtures, **/testdata. Up to {{max}}.
secret_rules.allow_stopwords: When the value contains one of these words
secret_rules.allow_stopwords_help: One per line, 3 characters or more: example, dummy, changeme. Up to {{max}}.
secret_rules.reason_required: Explain why you're changing the settings (at least 5 characters).
secret_rules.reason_placeholder: Why (kept in the history), e.g. “Test fixtures use fake Stripe keys”
secret_rules.effect: Changes apply from the next scan. A silenced secret isn't hidden: it moves to Excluded with the setting that withheld it and no longer counts as open. If it's real, rotate it first.
secret_rules.allowlist_help: For values that aren't real credentials: test fixtures, examples, placeholders.
secret_rules.opt_in_help: This rule flags any URL with a user and password in it, so it mostly catches documentation examples and local connection strings. Turn it on if your code may hold real connection strings with credentials. Hard-coded passwords are already checked by default.

scope.help: The current state of every asset in this scope, taken together: scans, PRs and imports. Open an asset to see its runs and settings.
scope.one_asset_only: Excluded paths, secret rules and picking a specific run work on one asset: choose “One” or open an asset under “By asset”.
scope.failed: Couldn't load the findings of this scope: {{error}}
scope.open_gone: That asset is no longer among the analyzed ones.
scope.truncated: Showing the {{shown}} most urgent of {{total, number}} findings in this tab. The figures count them all; narrow the scope to list the rest.

scope.triage_partial_other: Saved in {{count, number}} of {{total, number}} assets. These failed:

control.held_one: {{number}} finding kept open since {{date}}: the scan that day would have marked too many fixed at once. The next complete scan that confirms it closes it.
control.held_other: {{number}} findings kept open since {{date}}: the scan that day would have marked too many fixed at once. The next complete scan that confirms them closes them.
control.release_confirm: They're marked fixed without waiting for the next complete scan to confirm it. Do it only if you know they're gone.
control.unverified_one: {{number}} finding hasn't been checked in {{scans}} scans or more: its engine failed or didn't read where it was. Look at the steps of the last scans.
control.unverified_other: {{number}} findings haven't been checked in {{scans}} scans or more: their engines failed or didn't read where they were. Look at the steps of the last scans.
control.held_reason_one: {{number}} finding kept open since {{date}}: the scan on {{tripped}} would have marked {{fixed}} of {{open}} open findings fixed at once, past the safety limit (at least {{minimum}} findings and {{percent}} of those open). The next complete scan that confirms it closes it.
control.held_reason_other: {{number}} findings kept open since {{date}}: the scan on {{tripped}} would have marked {{fixed}} of {{open}} open findings fixed at once, past the safety limit (at least {{minimum}} findings and {{percent}} of those open). The next complete scan that confirms them closes them.
control.configuration_one: {{number}} finding wasn't checked: the scan's configuration changed, so its absence proves nothing. It stays open and doesn't count toward any indicator; its detail says what changed. Turn the rule or engine back on in the scan settings, or mark it fixed if you know it's gone.
control.configuration_other: {{number}} findings weren't checked: the scan's configuration changed, so their absence proves nothing. They stay open and don't count toward any indicator; each one's detail says what changed. Turn the rule or engine back on in the scan settings, or mark them fixed if you know they're gone.

ai_prompt.help: Paste it into Claude, Cursor or Copilot: it has the rule, where it is, the code shown above when there is some (with its secrets hidden), and the fix. Pitangus doesn't send it anywhere.
ai_prompt.failed: Couldn't copy it: select the text below and copy it by hand.

code.title: Code
code.loading: Reading the code from the repository…
code.error: Couldn't read the code right now.
code.read_now: Read from the repository at the scanned commit just now. Pitangus doesn't store your code.
code.read_now_masked: Read from the repository at the scanned commit just now, with the secrets found in this file hidden. Pitangus doesn't store your code.
code.masked_line: Line hidden: a secret was found on it

reason.secret: Pitangus never shows a secret's code, only where it is. Rotate it first, then remove it.
reason.imported: The code isn't shown for an imported finding: its file, line and commit came with the import, not from a Pitangus scan.
reason.symlink: The code isn't shown: this path is a symbolic link, and Pitangus never reads a file under another name.
reason.secret_other_commit: The code isn't shown: a secret was found in this file at another commit, and its lines may have moved since.
reason.local: The code isn't available here: this scan ran on a local folder. Open the file in your editor.
reason.no_commit: The code isn't available: this scan didn't record which commit it read.
reason.no_location: The code isn't available: the engine didn't say which line it is on.
reason.file_gone: The code isn't available: the repository no longer has this file at the scanned commit.
reason.file_changed: The code isn't available: the file is shorter than the lines this finding points at.
reason.binary: The code isn't available: it's a binary file.
reason.repository_gone: The code isn't available: the repository is no longer reachable with Pitangus's connection.
reason.repository_unreachable: The code isn't available right now: the repository couldn't be read.
